history.subject: 5 Nov 1895: George B. Selden granted US Patent 549,160 'Road-Engine' (The Henry Ford). Application filed 9 May 1879 (The Henry Ford inscription) -> ~16 years. Selden, a patent attorney, conceived but did not build a gasoline car in 1877 and 'shrewdly waited until 1895' (The Henry Ford). After an eight-year legal fight led by Henry Ford, the broad patent claim was severely restricted in 1911 (The Henry Ford). Not used: royalty figures/ALAM (not read this run).

facts.subject: Yanar Dag, Absheron peninsula near Baku: flames up to 3 m rise from a thin porous layer of sandstone (Wikipedia); natural gas seeping out (Wikipedia; Lonely Planet 'naturally escaping gas'). Some local accounts: discovered in the 1950s when a shepherd accidentally ignited it; others say it has burned for 4 000 years (Wikipedia; Lonely Planet: shepherd's cigarette in the 1950s vs 'unquenched for millennia') -> 'deyilənə görə'. Marco Polo (13th c.) wrote about natural gas flames in the region (Wikipedia + Lonely Planet). State reserve by presidential decree 2 May 2007 (Wikipedia). Not used: strip length (Wikipedia 15 m vs Lonely Planet 10 m), 'burns in rain' (not in body text).

facts.subject: Saturn's rings: the ring system extends up to 282 000 km from the planet but is about 10 m thick in most places; made mostly of water-ice particles from smaller than a grain of sand to as large as mountains (NASA/JPL PIA14943, 13 Aug 2018). Caltech Cool Cosmos: 282 000 km 'across', ~1 km thick -> thickness differs; we follow NASA/JPL and say 'çox yerdə'. Earth-Moon ~384 400 km -> 282 000 ≈ three quarters.

facts.subject: Lake Baikal, Siberia: more than 330 rivers and streams flow in (Britannica; Wikipedia 'as many as 330'); the only outflow is the Angara (both). Deepest lake: Britannica 1 620 m, Wikipedia 1 642 m -> '1 600 metrdən çox'. Age 20-25 million years (Britannica) / 25-30 (Wikipedia) -> '20 milyon ildən çox'. About one-fifth of the fresh water on Earth's surface (Britannica; Wikipedia 22-23% / 19% unfrozen). Baikal seal (nerpa) endemic (Wikipedia; Britannica 'the one mammal species').

facts.subject: Leyli and Majnun opera by Uzeyir Hajibeyli: first performed 12 Jan (O.S.) = 25 Jan 1908 at the Taghiyev Theatre in Baku (Wikipedia; preslib.az 25 Jan; azer.com + Azertag 12 Jan = Old Style). Considered the first opera of the Muslim East (Wikipedia, Azertag, preslib.az, azer.com). Hajibeyli was 22 (preslib.az, Azertag; azer.com says 23; born Sept 1885 -> 22). Muslim women could not appear on stage: all parts played by men (Azertag); Leyli was played by a young non-actor, Abdurrahim Farajov, who agreed on one condition - that no one discover who he was (preslib.az; azer.com: a tea-house waiter who dressed as a woman). Majnun: Huseyngulu Sarabski (all). Job conflict (chef's apprentice vs waiter) -> not stated.

trend.subject: NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory re-entered on Wed 4 Nov 2026 at 7:39 a.m. ET (12:39 GMT = 16:39 Baku) over North Sumatra, Indonesia, ~3.4N 98.6E (Xinhua 5 Nov, citing NASA; Space.com via ua.news 4 Nov, McDowell/US Space Force data). NASA expected most of the ~3 200 lb spacecraft to burn up, some parts may survive; risk to people ~1 in 2 100 (NASA blog 2-3 Nov). Launched 20 Nov 2004 (Wikipedia; NASA 'launched in 2004'), designed for a 2-year prime mission, worked 'almost 22 years' (NASA, Xinhua). Orbit decayed because higher solar activity expanded the atmosphere (Wikipedia). Rescue: Katalyst LINK robotic tug ($30 M NASA contract, Space.com; launched 3 Jul 2026 on Pegasus XL) failed with attitude-control/propulsion problems (Xinhua, Space.com, Wikipedia). GRB 090423 at 13.035 billion light-years, then the most distant explosion seen (Wikipedia). Not used: '2 000+ GRBs' (only Space.com).
